summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a history of a failed renal transplant, and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted for symptomatic anemia with a pre-dialysis hemoglobin of 6.6 and reported fatigue and dyspnea. Her post-dialysis hemoglobin was 7.7, within her baseline range, but due to mild symptoms, she received one unit of packed red blood cells slowly overnight and tolerated it well without volume overload. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and no further dialysis was needed. Her atrial fibrillation was managed with home medications, and her subtherapeutic INR of 1.2 led to continued warfarin without bridging. The chronic itchy rash on her back was not acute, and she remained on clobetasol and hydroxyzine. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved hemoglobin, and instructions to continue all medications and monitor post-dialysis labs.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
Rash and other nonspecific skin eruption
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other parts of uterus
Acquired absence of both cervix and uterus
